svg.aria-label: Status epilepticus treatment algorithm by time

g.text: 0–5 min
Stabilization
ABCs, O2, position on side, time the seizure, cardiac monitor, IV access
Fingerstick glucose: if <60 mg/dL → thiamine 100 mg IV, then dextrose (D50)
Labs: BMP, Ca, Mg, CBC, ASM levels, tox screen, β-hCG
Definition of status: ≥5 min continuous or recurrent without recovery
5–20 min
Benzodiazepine
IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (max 4 mg/dose), may repeat once in 5–10 min
No IV: IM midazolam 10 mg (>40 kg; 5 mg if 13–40 kg) — equal or better (RAMPART)
Alternatives: IV diazepam 0.15–0.2 mg/kg; intranasal/buccal midazolam; rectal diazepam
Under-dosing benzodiazepines is the most common error
Second-line
One IV agent (equally effective, ESETT):
Levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (max 4500 mg) · Fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg (max 1500)
Valproate 40 mg/kg (max 3000 mg; avoid in pregnancy, liver disease)
Phenobarbital 15–20 mg/kg if none available
>40 min
Refractory
status
Intubate; ICU; continuous EEG (rule out nonconvulsive status)
Continuous infusion: midazolam, propofol, or pentobarbital (or ketamine)
Titrate to seizure suppression / burst suppression for 24–48 h
Search for cause: CT/MRI, LP (encephalitis), autoimmune panel
Not waking 20–30 min after convulsions stop → urgent EEG
